description: PROBES: candidate vocabularies with no measurement at all, where the whitelist's blind spot is made visible instead of silent. Every arm names a replication genre that carries NO replication vocabulary, so no amount of tuning the word "replicate" will ever reach it — revisiting/reconsidered titles (heavily used in economics), repeated-experiment and independent-test phrasings, external and out-of-sample validation, re-examination, the pre-2010 "we attempted to confirm the finding" framing that predates the stabilised vocabulary, and the many-analyst / adversarial-collaboration / forecasting-tournament genre whose abstracts describe the consortium rather than a replication. Nothing here has a count, a precision or a sample; that is the point of the rule. One clause per probe so each is separately attributable and can be promoted on its own count, never as a block. The arms are deliberately narrow rather than broad: an arm that fires on everything tells you nothing about the genre it was written for. Several are title-only for the same reason a title stem beats an abstract stem — "revisiting" in an abstract is ordinary discourse. The revisiting arm is one clause over the whole title rather than a title-initial and a title-anywhere pair, because the title-initial form is a strict subset of the other and two clauses where one contains the other cannot be counted apart; splitting "Revisiting X" from "X, revisited" is a narrowing to do once the arm has a count worth narrowing. Replication side only: the reproduction-side probes (`re-estimat*`, `reimplement*`, `rerun`, CODECHECK certificates, artifact-evaluation reports) are parked in rule_ideas.md for #155.
